MOOVICUT AGENT GUIDE

PURPOSE
Moovicut prepares an editable storyboard and shot list. It does not generate video. The website UI is in English, Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans), Portuguese, Japanese, French, German, Luxembourgish, and Italian. The header stores the choice as moovicut.language. ?lang= is the shareable form, and English omits it. Fixed prompt lines follow the site language. Optional promptLanguage defaults to en on the API, and JSON field names stay English.

BROWSER AUTOMATION
The open studio page (`/studio`) exposes window.Shotboard (window.Moovicut is the same object). Use capabilities() to inspect supported actions and getProject() to read the current project. createProject({ premise, model }) creates a storyboard. updateShot(id, patch), reorderShot(id, direction) and deleteShot(id) edit the board. exportJSON() returns a portable project document. This is an in-page API. The public network API is separate and stateless.

DEFAULT BOARD
A new board is 5 scenes × 3 seconds (15s total) unless shots, duration, or scenes say otherwise. A board longer than 40 shots is split into parts of at most 40 shots. The cut is the last scene boundary at or before that limit. One scene longer than 40 shots is cut at a shot boundary and marked `part_split_inside_scene`. Every part keeps the same film sheet and lock lines. `parts` is present only when there is more than one part. 30s is 10 × 3s. 60s is 20 × 3s. Step-by-step mode in /studio edits each scene. Agents pass the same controls to POST /api/v1/storyboard or the MCP tool plan_storyboard.

REMOTE API
POST /api/v1/storyboard accepts premise, model, shots, mode or sequenceMode, continuity, density, prompt_style (short or detailed; short is the default per-shot video prompt: framing, the named action, the full lock line, the place, one light, and locked-off camera unless a movement was set, and the lock line is pasted unchanged; detailed keeps the full sheet and the same lock line), optional promptLanguage or prompt_language (en, zh-Hans, pt, ja, fr, de, lb, it; omitted means en), aspectRatio, genre, style, duration, compact, an optional scenes array, a scenario object or text, input "prose", and the light presets ad, series, and explainer. Free prose is split on place and time cues unless splitScenes is false. The current firm place wins, and a sentence with no listed verb is kept. An article inside a venue name is not a place cue. The cuts array gives each cue and reason. A detected character with no look is a warning, not a 400. A sentence that only describes a person fills the character sheet and is not a shot. Age and a carried item stay in the lock line. A story with no named place still plans, and that place is marked uncertain. Time of day applies from the sentence that states it, forward only. A later first name aliases the full name. A part's place and time are its first shot. A place noun used only as an object does not move the scene. An explicit names-only scenario is still 400. Scenario mode stores characters, places, and light once, resolves them in each generated prompt, packs 15–60s sequences, and warns from 6,000 characters (hard cap 8,000). Style families are anime (manga is an alias), cinema, and documentary, and they lock the style in every mode, including a plain premise. An unknown family is 400. A shot marked promptEdited, including a client prompt or a posted shotboard.compact.v1 board, is kept unless overwritePrompt is true. Series is 3 to 8 episodes and three shots each, so the default of 3 episodes is 9 shots. The rate limit uses Railway's X-Real-IP, ignores X-Forwarded-For, and counts across connections. A repeated model warning such as Sora's long-clip note is returned once per board. Ad turns product and benefit into hook, hero, proof, and pack shot, with the product locked on the film sheet. Series plans 3 to 8 vertical episodes on one film sheet. Explainer turns a numbered list into one action per shot and snaps duration to the selected model profile. A premise that does not use the Name, trait, trait shape is not turned into a scenario. That shape keeps the named people, splits look and outfit, and uses the real action sentences as shots. input prose reads English and French only, does not call a model, and returns those shots, or HTTP 400 with error and a message that lists each missing piece. Text in another language stays as written. A names-only scenario object is 400 and the message names each missing field. splitActions defaults to true and splits a multi-action shot; false keeps it in one shot. format agent includes warnings when a shot looks risky. He walks away is one action and is not too_many_actions. A scene whose only names are public figures, brands, or trademarks returns the neutral risk note and does not add missing-character or missing-place lines. regenerateShot plus project rebuilds one shot and leaves the others unchanged. warnings is omitted when empty and never blocks the board. Every mode shares one film sheet, and switching modes keeps it. format "agent" returns shotboard.compact.v1. Minified JSON, with no extra whitespace, is the token-efficient way to send that compact document. A scenario may omit premise; the idea line is then the character and place names, not the first scene's action. A browser library can export characters, places, and styles. model accepts grok, google, sora, kling, runway, luma, wan, or generic. A full response includes modelProfile with the cited sources. Veo accepts 4, 6, or 8 seconds and 16:9 or 9:16. Values the official page does not state are marked unverified. compact:true or ?compact=1 returns title, premise, model, aspectRatio, studioUrl, and shots of order, duration, and prompt. studioUrl is a /studio#board= link. The hash is not stored.
GET /openapi.json is the OpenAPI 3.1 document.
POST /mcp is stateless MCP (initialize, tools/list, tools/call). Tools: plan_storyboard, export_prompts, validate_storyboard. GET /mcp describes it. /.well-known/mcp.json is discovery.
GET /agents and /agents.md explain when to use each one.
No API key. 30 requests per minute per IP. No database. Premises are not stored.
Custom scenes example:
{"premise":"A lighthouse keeper races the dusk to repair a failing beacon.","model":"grok","scenes":[{"action":"Wide view of the lighthouse at dusk","duration":3,"camera":"Slow push-in","lighting":"Blue hour"},{"action":"Close on the keeper repairing the lens","duration":4,"notes":"Wind on the gallery"}]}

CLI
node cli/moovicut.mjs --premise "A lighthouse keeper races the dusk." --model google --output storyboard.json
node cli/moovicut.mjs --premise "A lighthouse keeper races the dusk." --model google --shots 4 --duration 3 --output storyboard.json
node cli/moovicut.mjs --input storyboard.json --export-prompts
The shotboard command runs the same program. Omitting --shots and --duration plans 5 scenes of 3 seconds.

DOCUMENT CONTRACT
The flat shotboard.v1 document includes id, title, premise, model/target_model, aspectRatio and shots. Each shot includes a stable id/shot_id, numeric order, framing, lens, camera, action, lighting, sound, continuity, duration/duration_seconds and prompt. Preserve user-edited prompt text when reordering. Validate imported documents. Do not send prompts to a model unless the person chooses to paste them.

LOCAL STORAGE
Projects are stored in the current browser. JSON export is the portable backup. The studio can save a shotboard.backup.v1 library of projects on this device and restore that file after it validates. Browser storage failures must be reported, never hidden behind a success message.

PRICE
The prompts work with Grok Imagine, Google, or any other AI image or video model. Grok Imagine and Google are prompt targets in the picker, not bundled generation. Planning, editing, and JSON export are free. There is no subscription. Optional tips open https://buymeacoffee.com/enzoc1977r in a new tab. Moovicut does not take payment itself.

LIMITS
No account, no cross-device sync, and no video rendering inside Moovicut. The site is in English.
